cohort: 505 laboring mothers who underwent induction of labor at Al-Thora General Hospital in Yemen between June 2019 and January 2022.
finding: Multiparity, misoprostol use for induction, premature rupture of membranes (PROM), and oligohydramnios significantly predicted induction of labor success, while advanced maternal age, advanced gestational age, and higher baby weight increased the risk of IOL failure.
mod_finding: Following induction of labor, 87.9% of women achieved a vaginal birth, while 12.1% resulted in cesarean deliveries.
cross-section timing: Data was collected over a three-year period from June 2019 to January 2022.
birth_weight: Babies with weights between 2 and 4 kg were included in the analysis of IOL outcomes.
gest_age: Gestational ages between 37 and beyond 40 weeks were analyzed in relation to IOL outcomes.
